key_insight: Activating one x4 chip per access cuts row-activation energy about 8x for random graph and KV traffic, using commodity DRAM dies with only controller changes.
killer_doubt: The RCD broadcasts CA to every chip, so custom DIMMs are needed; 64 B from one x4 chip takes 128 beats (~20 ns); total energy falls ~1.5x, not 8x (estimate).
decisive_experiment: Ramulator/DRAMPower trace study (~$20k) of per-chip activation on graph and KV-cache traces, reporting total energy and tail latency against DDR5 32-bit subchannels.
prior_art: Mini-rank (Zheng et al., MICRO 2008), HP MC-DIMM (Ahn et al., 2009), single-subarray access (Udipi, ISCA 2010); DDR5 subchannels, HBM pseudo-channels [training knowledge].

key_insight: Spare whole tiers so tier-wide defects stop compounding with stack height. This is a useful yield feature for any 3D DRAM dossier, not a standalone invention.
killer_doubt: Through-hole and HAR-etch defects kill every tier in a string, so sparing cannot fix them; 20% more tiers means ~20% more deposition and a 20% deeper etch.
decisive_experiment: Monte Carlo yield model (~$50k) fed with published 3D-NAND defect classes: what share of killers is tier-wide versus through-hole, and the net cost/bit at 100+20 versus 100 tiers.
prior_art: Row/column/block redundancy is universal; 3D NAND uses dummy word lines and bad-block remapping; HBM has spare TSVs and channel repair [training knowledge].

key_insight: A buried-well CCD string has no access-transistor tail; only thermal generation drains packets. The insight holds only for a wide-gap channel, not for silicon.
killer_doubt: Poly or recrystallized Si has grain-boundary generation centres, giving ~1e3-1e5x c-Si dark current and ms-class retention at 85 C (estimate). Single-crystal vertical channels are unmanufacturable.
decisive_experiment: None needed separately. The IGZO CCD speed test under I-08879 supersedes it. If Si is still wanted, measure dark current on a laser-recrystallized poly-Si planar CCD at 85 C (~$100k).
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD memory (IEDM 2024 planar; IMW 2026 3D) chose a wide-gap channel (via search snippet); 1970s Si CCD memories (Intel, Fairchild).

key_insight: A 32-tier oxide CCD string gives ~2-4x 1b density with no capacitor, no access transistor and no EUV, in NAND-like process. This is the density-optimised point of the CCD family.
killer_doubt: imec is already on this path. Demonstrated clocks are 4-6 MHz, but a 32-bit, 4-phase string needs ~1 GHz (128 transfers) for <=130 ns access, a ~200x gap.
decisive_experiment: Merge into the I-08879 dossier. Same planar IGZO CCD test chip, plus a 32-64-bit string to measure cumulative CTE at 100 MHz-1 GHz and 85 C with fat zero.
prior_art: imec: planar 142-bit 4-phase IGZO CCD (IEDM 2024) and vertical 3-word-line 3D CCD (IMW 2026) for CXL buffer memory (via search snippet).

key_insight: Floating-diffusion gain lets a CCD well hold very little charge (~0.1 fF), so one hole etch serves many bits. Striping a line across 512 strings hides serial latency.
killer_doubt: 200 bits on 200 gates is impossible: a packet needs 2-4 gates, so it holds 50-100 bits. 600-800 transfers per rotation is ~100 us at imec's demonstrated 6 MHz.
decisive_experiment: Superseded by the I-08879 CCD speed/CTE test. Only revisit long strings if that test shows CTE >=0.99998 per transfer at >=500 MHz.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD memory claims DRAM-beating density at ~50 layers with multibit (IEDM 2024; 3D at IMW 2026) (via search snippet).

key_insight: Short 8-16-bit oxide CCD strings latched to SRAM keep DRAM-class latency, with no capacitor, access transistor, EUV or per-tier contact. They tolerate CTE 0.999, which long strings cannot.
killer_doubt: Clock speed. imec shows >6.25 MHz planar and >4 MHz 3D; a ~20 ns string read needs ~1 GHz phase clocks (24-32 transfers). Trap-limited CTE at GHz is unmeasured.
decisive_experiment: Planar 16-32-gate IGZO/IGO 4-phase CCD with segmented low-R gates at a university fab (~$300k), RF-probed. Measure CTE versus clock from 10 MHz to 1 GHz, at 25/85 C, with and without fat zero.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD (IEDM 2024: 142 bits, >98% CTE, >200 s, >1e10 cycles; IMW 2026 3D) targets CXL buffer, not DRAM latency (via search snippet).

key_insight: Tie every same-phase tier together: the 128-tier stack needs 3-4 contacts instead of a 128-step staircase, removing a major 3D cost module. Fold this into the I-08879 dossier.
killer_doubt: The claimed 128 ns worst case for 384 transfers implies a 3 GHz phase clock, ~500x imec's demonstrated 6 MHz. A whole block shifts on every access.
decisive_experiment: In the I-08879 test chip, add an 8-16-tier vertical stack with phase-tied planes (partner 200 mm line, ~$250k). Measure plane RC, shift energy per bit and CTE versus block size.
prior_art: imec 3D CCD uses word lines as phase gates (3-WL vertical holes, IMW 2026) (via search snippet); phase-tying of a tall stack was not checked.

key_insight: A NAND-topology string of 2T0C cells, with back-gate bypass so unselected read FETs act as pass gates, puts no capacitor or per-cell contact in each hole.
killer_doubt: 64 series IGZO FETs (~50-200 kOhm each) carry ~0.1-0.3 uA: 30-100 ns to develop 100 mV on 100 fF. Also needs two planes per tier and per-cell floating nodes.
decisive_experiment: Planar series strings of 8/16/32/64 dual-gate IGZO TFTs (~$150k). Measure string current, sense time and read disturb versus N and bypass voltage. TCAD the two-channel vertical hole.
prior_art: NEO 3D X-DRAM 1T1C/3T0C in a 3D-NAND-like flow (company-reported); IMECAS 4-layer 2T0C (VLSI 2026). No series-string gain cell found.

key_insight: Static inference weights do not need DRAM. A via-programmed BEOL ROM in a mature U.S. fab removes refresh and EUV for that share.
killer_doubt: Models churn every ~6-12 months. 16 decks means ~32 extra metal layers. An 8B, 4-bit model needs ~1.6e10 e-beam vias per die. Passive via crosspoints lack selectors.
decisive_experiment: MPW test chip (~$200k) of a 2-4-deck via-programmed capacitive crosspoint ROM measuring read margin, sneak paths and bits/mm², plus a cost model against LPDDR at model lifetimes of 6-24 months.
prior_art: Mask/via ROM (decades old); ROM-based CIM (e.g., YOLoC, DAC 2022); hardwired-model LLM ASICs (e.g., Taalas) [training knowledge].

key_insight: A whole DRAM wafer bonded under a wafer-scale processor adds ~2-3 TB at <0.3 pJ/bit. The processor's redundancy fabric absorbs the wafer-to-wafer compound-yield risk.
killer_doubt: Wafer-scale compute dissipates ~0.5 W/mm² (estimate), so the DRAM runs at >=85-95 C with 2-4x refresh. The market is one or two vendors, and $1M cannot build a wafer-scale demo.
decisive_experiment: Die-to-wafer hybrid-bond a DRAM test die onto a heater-equipped logic die at 2-6 um pitch (~$300k). Measure bond yield, pJ/bit and retention tails at 85-110 C under 0.5 W/mm².
prior_art: Xi'an UniIC SeDRAM hybrid-bonded DRAM-on-logic (IEDM 2020) [training knowledge]; DRAM-wafer-to-processor patents (US 11,430,766); study's N-41 carrier-is-memory.

key_insight: Injecting even ~40 stored electrons into a Geiger-mode junction triggers avalanche almost surely. Gain makes a few-electron bit readable. The value is as an EMCCD-style output stage for CCD strings.
killer_doubt: A 100-electron node may lose ~60 e per 64 ms, so leakage must be <=0.15 fA, ~90x below the Si tail. SPADs are µm-scale; bitline pitch is 30-40 nm.
decisive_experiment: TCAD plus a 65 nm SPAD test structure (~$200k) fed metered 10-100 e packets. Measure trigger probability versus dark counts in a 2 ns gate, and the minimum pitch.
prior_art: Impact-ionisation floating-body Z-RAM (Innovative Silicon); EMCCD gain registers; Fossum quanta-image-sensor jots read single electrons without avalanche [training knowledge]; study's N-04/N-84.

key_insight: A guard-driven T-switch zeroes drain-source voltage across the inner write FET, suppressing subthreshold leakage in Si gain-cell eDRAM. It is cheap to verify on an MPW.
killer_doubt: Junction, GIDL and gate leakage remain. A live source follower per cell draws static current. Realistic gain is ~10x, against IGZO's native ~1e3x lower off-current.
decisive_experiment: 28/40 nm MPW (~$150k) with 2T, 3T-guarded and 4T internal-feedback gain-cell arrays. Measure retention tails at 85 C, area and standby power per bit.
prior_art: Internal-feedback/leakage-compensated 4T gain cells (Teman, Meinerzhagen, Burg et al., ~2014); T-switch in sample-and-hold circuits [training knowledge].
